assets.initial_prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: one finished botanical planting instruction poster, portrait EXACT 9:16 aspect ratio, 1440 pixels wide by 2560 pixels tall. Opaque background. One poster only, not a mockup, no frame or surrounding room.
Audience: dryland restoration learners in southeastern Spain. Prototype for a future Planting Explorer. Restrained scientific watercolor with precise technical diagram lines and exceptionally clear typography. Warm off-white paper, dark forest-green typography, brown soil section, subtle blue water accents. Spacious editorial hierarchy. Readable moderate amount of text, never tiny paragraphs.
Composition: small header and species title at top; small mature above-ground habit vignette in upper right labelled "Mature habit"; large central diagram of a YOUNG NURSERY PLANT being planted, with soil cutaway and intact root ball, thin precise leader lines and dimension arrows. Clearly distinguish mature habit vignette from young installation diagram. Below the main cross-section, a smaller separate conceptual root-pattern inset; footer three short practical checks and an establishment-water note. All root drawings schematic, not claimed measured distributions.
No arbitrary centimetres, metres, root-depth estimates, watering litres, spacing numbers, calendar claims, fertilizer recipes, exotic landscaping, logo, decorative stock icons or invented extra instructions. Do not portray a fully mature plant inside a tiny planting pit. NO plastic pot remaining in planted hole. Do not depict a waterlogged pit or gravel drainage layer. All annotations must point accurately to the structure named. All typography crisp, dark, legible with margins.

Species: carob / ALGARROBO, Ceratonia siliqua. Correct mature tree has a broad rounded evergreen crown, sturdy trunk, pinnate leaves with broad oval leathery leaflets; optional a few brown curved carob pods only in mature habit. Young plant has a slender woody stem and several correctly pinnate leaves, not simple oak leaves.
Main installation section: root collar/first woody roots at final soil surface, collar visible and unburied; root ball resting on firm undisturbed ground. Hole sides slope outward, broad shallow hole, about 2–3 times root-ball width as general tree guidance. The intact nursery root ball is distinct, with branching roots inside, no spiralled/coiled taproot and no roots drawn cut by the hole. No roots drawn below the firm base in installation panel. W horizontal arrow spans ROOT BALL only; H vertical arrow spans from first woody-root level to ball base. Wider width arrow spans the hole. Ground surface continuous, no mound against stem. Small root-pattern inset separately shows a carob seedling's descending primary root and branching lateral roots without depth scale; label nursery stock alters shape, no suggestion roots must be pruned.
Verbatim text to integrate naturally:
"PLANTING EXPLORER · EXAMPLE 01"
"ALGARROBO"
"Ceratonia siliqua"
"Carob · Evergreen tree"
"Mature habit"
"PLANTING GEOMETRY"
"Keep the root collar visible"
"Final soil level"
"W"
"H"
"Hole width: 2–3 × W"
"General tree guidance; adapt to soil and stock"
"Firm base · avoid settling"
"W = root-ball width"
"H = base to first woody roots"
"Root pattern · schematic"
"Primary root + woody laterals"
"Nursery stock changes root form"
"CHECK BEFORE PLANTING"
"Healthy roots · Free drainage · Space for mature crown"
"ESTABLISHMENT WATER"
"Wet the root ball and surrounding soil."
"Use a site-specific watering plan."
"Schematic, not to scale · Sources and watering notes supplied separately"
No extra literal text.

Species: PALMITO, Chamaerops humilis, Mediterranean fan palm. Mature vignette is a LOW CLUMPING fan palm with multiple short fibrous brown stems, palmate fan leaves divided into many stiff segments and spiny petioles. NOT a tall coconut/date palm, no feather leaves. Main installation is a small container-grown juvenile with a few partly divided fan leaves and a compact basal stem; not an adult cut trunk. Palm has adventitious roots from root-initiation zone, NOT a central taproot, no woody tree root flare. Keep intact root ball with many similar-calibre tan branching roots. Carefully draw root-initiation zone at stem base immediately below soil surface, enclosed by soil, with growing crown well above grade. Do not draw a fixed numeric depth; callout must say confirm the depth for supplied stock. Root-shoot interface must not be left exposed in midair; stem not deeply buried. Firm base beneath root ball, no roots below it in installation panel. W arrow ROOT-BALL width only, H arrow ROOT-BALL height only; broad hole about 2×W indicated as general container-palm guidance, not species-specific fixed rule. A separate root-pattern inset illustrates many adventitious roots arising from broad basal stem; no taproot. Short note distinguishes this from tree root collar.

Species: ESPARTO / ATOCHA, Macrochloa tenacissima (= Stipa tenacissima). This is a Mediterranean perennial bunchgrass, not a palm or shrub. Mature vignette dense coarse tussock of very long narrow tightly rolled wiry grey-green leaves arching outward from a thick basal mass of persistent straw-coloured leaf sheaths, optional few slim narrow straw inflorescences, not feathery pampas plumes.
Main installation: SMALL nursery-grown grass plug with a modest tuft of narrow wiry leaves. Crown/basal growing point at final soil surface, not buried in a deep pit. Compact cohesive plug contains many fine fibrous roots, no carrot root, bulb or woody trunk. Planting hole fitted to actual plug with some backfill space at sides, no invented numeric width multiplier. W arrow spans actual plug width, H actual plug height, arrow to firm base. Clearly caption this as a nursery-plug concept, actual stock must be confirmed (local library has no verified stock format). No uprooted wild mature clump. Roots in installation diagram inside plug only. A separate root-pattern inset shows grass crown with very dense slender fibrous roots spreading and descending, all approximate no metric depth or perfect spherical root cage. Inset label distinguish crown from palm stem.
